Per our conversation I put together a lightweight cost-verification playbook so your procurement and SRE teams can validate the token economics that will drive the POC acceptance criteria. Attached: HelixMAP-CostChecklist.xlsx (short worksheet) and a sample token export (POC-token-samples.txt).

High-level ask: can you confirm the expected average input prompt size and the target response length for the POC (ballpark tokens/user)? We want to validate three hypotheses in the MAP:
- tokens/$ at the projected POC QPS
- effective hit-rate from prefix/KV cache assumptions
- batching/window sizing tradeoffs for latency vs unit cost

Proposed timeline (can compress if you need faster close):
1) This week: confirm token sizes + procurement checklist items
2) Week of May 6: Redwood SE runs a 48-hour synthetic run against our POC model variant and returns the baseline econ report
3) Week of May 13: joint review + finalize mutual action plan and procurement steps

If it helps, Karthik (cc'd) can jump on a short technical call to walk through caching and batching assumptions.

Next step: could you drop estimated tokens per user and preferred go/no-go date for the POC?

Thanks,

Hi Sarah — looping in some concrete numbers so your SRE/procurement teams can validate quickly. Below are the model and runtime assumptions I used in the attached MAP-Cost-Model-v2.csv. We can adjust them if your instrumented samples differ.

1) Token sizing (based on your estimate: 320 prompt / 220 resp):
   - median round-trip tokens = 540 tokens/request
   - sample variance: 95% < 900 tokens per request

2) Cost per 1K tokens (hosted baseline for our recommended open model variant):
   - inference: $6.00 per 1M tokens => $0.006 per 1K tokens (example pricing used for POC econ calc)
   - effective model cost per request = 0.54 * $0.006 = $0.00324 per request (540 tokens = 0.54k)

3) Caching / prefix reuse assumptions (important for MAP):
   - prefix cache hit-rate scenarios: conservative 10% | expected 35% | aggressive 60%
   - when a prefix hits cache we avoid re-encoding the shared prefix tokens and skip KV fetch for that portion — effective tokens billed drop by ~prefix_length_used/total_tokens
   - for structured patient templates we typically see higher reuse; please share an anonymized sample and I can run an exact estimate

4) Batching behavior and latency tradeoffs:
   - continuous batching window default: 20ms (recommended for clinician UX) => modest batching boost, ~1.15x token-efficiency at your expected QPS
   - larger window (50-100ms) can improve tokens/$ by an additional ~1.3-1.6x but adds tail latency which may be visible to clinicians during peak flows

5) POC throughput math (peak numbers):
   - peak 40 QPS => 40 * 540 tokens/s = 21,600 tokens/s => ~1.296M tokens/min
   - at $0.006 per 1K tokens => peak cost estimate = 21.6k * $0.006 = $129.60 per second (note: convert units carefully in shared sheet)

6) Suggested MAP checks we recommend your team include:
   - instrumented token histogram from real traffic (we can help create a simple logging shim)
   - a caching pilot with a representative prefix sample to measure real hit-rate over 48 hours
   - one-run with conservative batching window (20ms) and one run with 80ms to capture latency impact

Attachments referenced: MAP-Cost-Model-v2.csv (detailed calc), POC-token-samples.txt (your sample + synthetic variations). I uploaded the cost model and a short playbook to the shared doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1XHelixMAPplaybook

Next step proposal: 30-minute technical sync tomorrow at 10:00am PT to agree on sample export format and to schedule the 48-hour run. If that works I will provision the POC runner and post a readout template.
